chapter_title: Đại Kết Cục Thứ Một Nghìn

anchor_types.R2: source-backed cultural/linguistic pattern with explicit variation
anchor_types.F1: fictional scene compatible with locked reality anchors

anchors.statement: Economic reforms launched with Đổi Mới in 1986 helped drive rapid economic and social transformation in Viet Nam.
anchors.use: intergenerational contrast, changing living standards, infrastructure, education and economic expectations

anchors.statement: Viet Nam officially connected to the global Internet on 19 November 1997; early access used fixed-line infrastructure and limited speeds.
anchors.use: Internet cafés, early home/commercial connectivity, rapid change in information access

anchors.statement: ADSL broadband entered the Vietnamese market in 2003, marking a shift from narrowband access toward higher-speed Internet; VNNIC reports about 3.1 million Internet users that year.
anchors.use: change in waiting time, Internet cafés/home access, faster information-seeking behavior without assuming universal household adoption

anchors.statement: General education curriculum renovation began around 2000, with revised national programs and textbooks launched from the 2002-03 school year; reform coexisted with teacher-led and memorization-heavy practices.
anchors.use: textbook-centered childhood scene, examination culture, tension between memorizing and understanding

anchors.statement: Viet Nam has been a WTO member since 11 January 2007.
anchors.use: later childhood/youth backdrop of accelerated international integration and household-level talk about work, prices, markets and foreign goods

anchors.statement: Vietnam inaugurated 3G in 2009; VNNIC's 25-year Internet timeline identifies the PC-to-mobile shift as a major change in Internet usage habits around this period.
anchors.use: Internet beginning to travel with users rather than remaining tied mainly to desktop/location-based access; faster multi-context communication

anchors.statement: Vietnamese person reference commonly uses kin terms even outside genealogical kinship, indexing relative age/generation and social relationship.
anchors.use: dialogue, social relation encoded in forms such as anh/em/cô/chú/bác/cháu

anchors.statement: Tết is a major Vietnamese celebration associated with family reunion, greetings, visits and ancestor-related practices, with contextual variation.
anchors.use: intergenerational storytelling, family memory and social ritual

anchors.statement: Viet Nam experienced rapid urbanization alongside growth; World Bank analyses describe motorbikes as a dominant personal transport mode in major-city mobility during the period under discussion.
anchors.use: street soundscape, alleys, mobility, migration and changing urban texture
